t: Find out about June Ruins from Negus Sukhitep on the shore near the Imperial camp.

Communication channel? Let me think. I have an idea... A scientist that was attached to our crew, Negus Sukhitep, found some old June ruins near our camp. Frankly, we don't care about them, we don't have working Adventurer's Stones anyway, but they may be useful to you. So go to our scientist and find out the latest news from him. Perhaps studying the ruins will yield some benefits?
Don't interrupt me. I am trying to understand why these ruins don't work.
What? How did you do it? I lost my head trying to figure out how to rouse the ancient magic in this stone, but you did it with a single touch!
Contact Yasker using the subspace communicator and receive further instructions.

All right, wait. I will try to understand the structure of the spell. All June teleportation stones were assigned to old world coordinates and this stone is probably no exception.
Triangulation... Adjustment of two minutes... Dislocation of 1.5 degrees due south by southwest... Aha! Here it is!
Some strange results. This place is recorded as "Irdrich," but this is the first time that I hear about this allod. I think I saw some mention in the ancient records of a legendary island hidden among sharp reefs, and therefore inaccessible to navigators of that time. But there were no Great Mages, which means that the island should have dissolved in the Astral long-long time ago. Strange. We should probably report this to Yasker immediately! But don't try to do it right here! Secrecy above all!
Well, what happened to you? As a matter of fact, I have a top secret meeting to attend!

Irdrich? No, never heard about such an allod. Perhaps if we check the old records, then something might be cleared up.
However, this is not important right now. As I understand it, you weren't able to find the evidence of Tep's presence yet? Then you haven't searched hard enough! I don't believe that our recon data is erroneous and our scouting is for naught. It seems like you are not looking in the right place.
Teleport to the Demon Hunters' ship, return to Irdrich and relay Yasker's orders to Leonid Brelin.

Right now it is important to determine whether or not the sector where you currently are is cut off from our world.
The demons' activity has drawn the Hunters' attention; their battleship is cruising near the wormhole. I've already received a preliminary assessment of the situation from them. I must say that they are better at studying the Astral than us and the League. Anyway, they state that the wormhole entrance is ringed into an energy loop and going through it might drain energy from any object, be it a reactor or a human. This is what you experienced when you fainted. Don't ask how such an anomaly was created. There are many theories and not enough facts. But everyone agrees that your chances returning the same way are nil. Therefore, we should utilize good old teleportation.
I'll try to tune my Adventurer's Stone to the portal on the deck of the Hunters' flagship. Try to teleport there and enter the wormhole again. If my conjectures are correct, then the maximum risk is a loss of consciousness. I certainly hope that you don't manage to break your neck doing that...
And relay my order to the most senior able-bodied officer: Don't stop searching for Tep. We cannot wage war on two fronts without any verifiable information!
So, were you able to contact the capital?

So that's how it is? Continue with the assigned mission, despite the fact that nothing remains of the strike squadron? Hell of a job for us! When the Motherland says "do it," our only answer is "yes!"
Show the strange map to Cha Pie-Pie.

So... Let me think. No, I am definitely not familiar with the map legend. Besides, I've never heard of the League's military creating operation maps on a lousy papyrus, where all legends are stupid doodles, written in coal. It is probably the work of our potential enemies: Glittering Wing tribe.
You know what? Take this map to Cha Pie-Pie. He probably knows what is shown on it.
Quarr, wingless one! What do you want? I'm a bit busy right now. I have to prepare a patriotic speech for my warriors. Your wise wingless Igor advised me so.
Meet Elchana Speak-with-Spirits on Kahlua Island.

Did you find this map in the enemy camp? Did you take it away from wingless spies that call themselves League? Bad news for all of us.
I believe you. Scouts detected a strange small furry creature monitoring our city. They also saw a white-winged creature near it. The map confirms my concerns. It shows our patrols, fortifications, all passages and exits. This map obviously was drawn by white aviaks. If white-winged ones ally with League, we'll be in trouble. They will bury the fruit of our revolution deep in the ground. That cannot happen!
I, Cha Pie-Pie, on behalf of working people, state: Steel Claw and wingless outlanders must form an alliance. We see that future belongs to a just and honest country, and that is our strength!
But we cannot enter into treaty without blessing of elements. Wind that carry us, earth that give us shelter, sea that feed us, and fire that burn in our dwellings all are our patrons. Only Elchana-Speak-with-Spirits understands them. She lives on Kahlua Island, to the east of our town. You, Son of the Wind, should go ask Elchana to talk to spirits. I've spoken my word, let them speak theirs.

Ah, wingless outlander did come see me. Let me guess... Cha Pie-Pie send you! He wants our spirits to bless alliance with outlanders that came from the great void? All right... You shall hear their word!
Meet Yasskul Naboo on the Isle of Singing Water.

So, the Copper Isle... Irdrich... See, the problem is that I sent a recon team to monitor the League, and they report that the League's military is in dire situation, like us. Without navy and support. What conclusion can we draw? A very simple one! If the League's military lured us into this sector, they did not expect that getting out of here would be rather... problematic.
Anyway, the side that works out the nature of this anomaly will strengthen its influence and dictate its terms. And, naturally, that has to be our great Empire!
In addition to everything, our squadron had separate research projects. We had several scientists attached to us, Yasskul Naboo and her assistants. They are conducting research now and are in need of a trusted person. I, as you understand, cannot send some storm trooper oaf to conduct such delicate research, so I need to enlist your help to assist the scientists. Success of this research is an important task and its solution will be for the benefit of the Empire!
Oh you clumsy oaf, where the hell have you... Oh! excuse me! I thought you were one of my assistants that I sent to the Astral shore to record measurements.
Meet the chief of Steel Wing tribe, Cha Pie-Pie, in the village of red aviaks in Rumbling Bay.

Do you know what is the main weapon of the Empire? It is not blades and bows, not astral ship cannons, not destructive spells of the Great Mages, not at all! The main weapon of the Empire is the enduring belief in its own righteousness. Ideology of our great country is dear and clear to everyone, from a scientist to the worker bee, from the wise Arisen to the dumbest goblin. And where weapons are powerless, our beliefs will bring us victory!
You're probably trying to guess what I'm getting at? You see, thanks to our ideology, we already found allies on this hostile earth. They are aviaks!
We met the local aviaks right after the crash and quickly found a common ground. Their country recently split when the aviaks that were dissatisfied with the local "aristocracy" rebelled and unanimously unseated the tyrants. Good for them! To each according to his needs, from each according to his ability! A citizen is valued for his labor, not his titles!
Anyway, right now there is a smoldering war raging between two tribes of a once united people, and with our help, our red allies - Steel Claw tribe - have all the chances to win. And then we will deal with the League with a joint force.
Hear my command! Go to the village of our allies and meet their chief, red commander Cha Pie-Pie. And try to gain his respect!

Quarr, wingless one!
Do you also think that honest work is the metric of respect? Good! But your heart is closed to a song of the wind... I see it. You cannot fly and you can never understand our people. If you want to speak with our people, you must learn to talk to wind spirits. You should go to Cheeba and learn, only then we can talk!
Pass all trials given by Cliff Master and meet Fire Master on the Ashy Wasteland.

Khurr... A sand speck is no dust. A flintstone! Good job... Hasty. Fussy. Dumb. Impatient. But hard. So, a sand speck or a flintstone? I must know...
Hurh... Let's test a send speck. Try it. No hurry. If it succeed, let it meet Brother. He is hasty and hot-headed as well. A flintstone will like him.
Umm... Brother lives far, on Azure atoll. He called me. Why should I? The earth is everywhere.
Humm... Go. I bless you. A fast sand speck, willing to understand the earth better. Will it? It can't go wrong. Go.
Ha ha ha! I knew you'd come!
You cannot extinguish the flame burning in the heart. Ha! The flame that you may help to fan will burn this whole boring world!
Destroy 12 mad boulders on the Ashy Wasteland and report your success to Cliff Master.

Humm... Hmm... A sand speck. Trying to understand a mountain. Amusing. Very. Ho ho ho.
Rocks will crush a fool. Earth will swallow. Fertilizer... OK, let the sand speck try.
Humm... Earth varies. Soft. Hard. Fertile. Barren. Calm. Quaking. It can be also alive. Dust specks call them spirits.
Humm... Spirits vary. Kind. Evil. Mad. I don't need the mad ones. They roll. Here and there. Thunder. Won't let you sleep.
Umm... A sand speck is weak. Mad ones are too. Equal opponents. Let the sand speck turn mad ones to dust. I don't like fuss...
Hurh... Dumb rolling boulders. They don't understand their purpose.
Humm... Rumblers don't rumble anymore. So quiet. Good. Not a sand speck, but a flintstone. Small. Hard. Calm. Good.
Plant a seed at the Ashy Wasteland and teach the Scorched Treant a lesson. Afterwards return to Cliff Master to report your victory.

Hurh... Earth is bad here. Tasteless. Smells burnt.
Umm... Plants are alive. They feel pain. Afraid of death. Scared of fire. Fear is rooted deep. Very deep. Nothing grows anymore. Nothing. Earth is scared...
Homm... A sand speck can help. Plant a seed. Say the magic word. A stem will sprout. It'll be evil. Very. It will absorb the earth's evil.
Ooh... The stem will sprout. It'll be wicked. It will absorb earth's wickedness. Strike it. Strike the wicked out of it. It'll become peaceful. Calm. It'll return to the earth. Bring appeasement. It will grow roots. Forest will grow. Not right away. Earth is patient. It can wait. Go.
Ooh... Earth has been patient for long. But if it angers, it is unstoppable...

Humm... Evil. Was. Gone. Good. A sand speck is light, but it fell on the proper side of the scale.
Hurr... Patience. Is altruism. Everything else decays. Time conquers all things.
Summon the earth spirit by touching an ancient menhir and help it clear the scorched areas of the Ashy Wasteland, then report your success to Cliff Master.

Hurh... A sand speck is still here? Annoying sand speck. Fussy. Lives fast. Hurries somewhere. Why? Stupid...
Homm... Very well. Let the impatient sand speck be useful. Earth is tired. Long time ago a fire occurred here. Many things were scorched. It is time for new things to grow. The shadow remains inside earth. It does not let new life start. Must be cleansed. We can wait. But a sand speck is in a hurry. Let it help, then.
Hurh... Menhir. Ancient. Protects the power of inceptive life. If you touch, it will release. It will breathe new life into the earth. Go.
Humm... Hurries. Everyone hurries. Where? Why? Hurry slowly. Then you will be prompt.
Hurr... Mountains turn into seas. Rivers into ranges. The important thing is to wait...
Humm... I hear. I see. Earth is blooming. Again. Good.
Meet with Wind Master at the Seven-Winds Cliff.

I heard the call! Wind Master is calling you. He is the kindest of all elements, always looks after our winged people. He lives where the wind eternally sing its sorrowful song among grey cliffs, and sea foam from waves flies into the air and falls in thousands of droplets. His voice is menacing, but be not afraid of him. Wind Master will not harm his children. He is merciful and just. If you receive his blessing, it will be easier later!
Mortal... You have no wingsss, but you hear my voice... You are truly the Ssson of the Wind!
Pass all the Fire Master's trials, return to Elchana on Kahlua Island and report that all the spirits of the elements gave their blessing.

Listen to me, creature of zest. Wind, water, earth and fire gave you a bit of their wisdom. I hope now you understand us, our ways, and our purpose. Ha! I wouldn't want our efforts to be futile. In the end, the purpose of our trials was just that. We don't care about squabbles of sentient beings and those who sent you for the elements' blessings; they can war with whoever they want. What we are interested in is you!
We sensed the hidden strength in you, strength that is more advanced than that of your clansmen, and we wanted to meet you. We wanted to understand who you are and give you the opportunity to understand us. My brother have drawn the conclusions. Now it's my turn to test you.
After you finish my task, go to the witch and tell her that they can butcher each other all they want! Ha ha ha!
Did spirits give their blessing? Good news, outlander!
Collect 5 units of tapir tallow, 5 bundles of dry brushwood, and use them to kindle a big fire out of a small one that burns near Fire Master on the Azure Atoll.

My brothers... are boring! Wind can only whistle and mindlessly wander to and fro. Water can only murmur something philosophic. It is trying to show itself as wise! Stone is slow-thinking and lazy. Not one of them understands life! Remember, fire is life! You are alive so long as you burn. When you are extinguished, you are dead. Ha! It is simple, like igniting a fire! Speaking of which, can you make bonfires? Not just bonfires, but a whole sea of fire, one that can be seen from the sky? No? It is very entertaining!
There are lots of fat tapirs around. So fat that they can barely walk. Their fat will make the flames shoot sky high. Ooh! Only throw in some logs. Plenty of those around as well!
Fire is alive, understand? If you don't feed it, it will die. But if you feed it regularly, it will be sky high!

Ah! I love the smell of ashes in the morning! Ha ha ha!
Oh, you are good, not even scared of all-consuming flame. I like you, hero. I swear by absolute zero, we will be friends!
Lure to the bonfire on the Azure Atoll and sacrifice 5 leopards, then boast about it to Fire Master.

So... What to do for fun now? What do you think, creature of flame? Burn? Ha ha! Outstanding idea! Of course, burn!
Burn is good. However, burning for the sake of burning is boring. Let me think... I got it!
Huge leopards live here. Toothy, predatory and spotted. Hot blood, flaming heart! Would you sacrifice them to the flame? Or shall I feed you to it? Ha ha ha! Don't be afraid, I am kidding! I like you! Just lure these big kitties to the burning bonfire and let the flame consume their beastly blood!

I am worshipped like a god. I am offered sacrifices. They think it will make me merciful! Ha ha ha! Fire cannot be merciful. It ignites to burn, not to lick hands like a stupid puppy. It can be a friend or an enemy, but flame will always be flame!

Eenie, meenie, miney moe.
Catch a tiger by the toe.
If he hollers, let him go.
 Eenie, meenie, miney moe.
...
What, not a tiger, but a leopard? Oh, you ruined the nursery rhyme...
...
 Eenie, meenie, miney meil.
Catch a tiger by the tail.
 If he hollers, let him be.
 Eenie, meenie, miney, me.
...
Now that's better! So what if it's not a tiger? The important thing is for the predator's blood to feed the flame with its power! Look how brightly and merrily it burns! Ha ha ha!
Find the screaming squawker, kill it and bring its heart to Fire Master.

Birds, birds... I don't like birds! My hissing and whistling brother spoils these loud creatures that poop from the sky, but I only acknowledge one kind of birds - fire birds. Ha!
Have you ever seen a rain of fire? It's when giant flames shoot from the earth's depths into the sky, like thousands of birds with fiery wings... A stunning spectacle... for those who understand the essence of fire! You do understand the essence of fire, don't you? Freedom is the answer! Freedom of desires, freedom of thoughts, freedom of actions. Say, I want to rip the heart out of a stupid winged creature that's always shooting at the mouth among the cliffs. Will you help me, creature of fire?
You can make a giant fire out of a small spark. It's beautiful!

Ha ha ha! Stupid bird will not annoy me anymore with its awful screams. Freedom, my sweet little flame. Someone is free to scream obscenities, and someone is free to break the neck and rip the heart from the chest of the stupid screamer. Know your abilities and your actions, lest you become hot ash, just like the heart of this stupid bird.
Rescue Torrick Hard-Luck from harpies that live on the Giant's Claw, by killing their leader, Shizgana.

Wingless one! Hail to Seven Winds! Will you help me? I really-really need help!
My beloved Torrick is gone. He is so unlucky! Trouble always finds him. And now he is in trouble again.
Harpies live on this island. Very wicked, insolent and loud. I hate them! They kidnapped my beloved to do something terrible. I think they want to marry Torrick to their leader, vile Shizgana! Such fate is worse than death!
I beg you, rescue my Torrick. He is so defenseless... But I love him more than life!
Poor, stupid Torrick. I'm always unlucky... Always in trouble!
Collect bright and shiny necklace gemstones that were eaten by hungry squawkers and bring them to Torrick Hard-Luck on the Giant's Claw.

I was going to my bride, beloved Gia. Then a black flock of harpies swooped in! They hit me in my beak and my eye and took my bag. The bag contained a present, a beautiful necklace. I've made it for the wedding. It took me a long time to make it! I wanted to give the necklace to Gia and ask her to marry me.
Dirty chickens are those harpies, they stole the bag and threw it atop the Giant's Claw. The bag opened, the necklace fell out and broke. Gems scattered everywhere. Hungry squawkers ate everything. Gems were beautiful and shiny. Squawkers swallowed all the gems!
Poor, poor Torrick! Now I have nothing to give my bride. It would be better if I die...
I was unlucky even in childhood. Even an egg with me inside always fell out of nest!

Did you find stones? Excellent!
...
Oh no... Stones are scratched and gnawed. Not shiny anymore. Again no luck for Torrick!
Collect a large squawker's egg and bring it to Torrick Hard-Luck on the Giant's Claw.

I know what to do! If wingless one helps me, I can save my love! I know where to get best present for my beloved Gia.
Huge squawkers inhabit Giant's Claw. Very ferocious. If you collect its egg, we may hatch the squawkling. The biggest, strongest and kindest squawker. I'm weak and cannot overcome a big squawker. But you surely can! Then I'll give an egg to Gia and help raise the best squawker in the tribe. Cheeba will be so jealous, he'll rip his tail feathers out!
Did you find a big egg? This is a very good gift!

Oh... Such a large egg... Gia will be excited! She will declare me a great hunter and agree to marry. Oh, I love Gia so much. More than life!
I'm very thankful to you wingless one. There are no words to express my gratitude!
Find the pirate ship's crew lost in the jungle, then tell Bell the Forester on the Rainbow Atoll about your success.

Oho! Hello! Where are you from? Then again, what's the difference?! We're all in the same deep doodoo here.
Whatcha staring at me for? Yes, I am a pirate. So what? Never seen one before? Pah! People usually see us either on the ship's deck or hanging from its mast. But now we're stuck here like landlubbers, dammit!
See, we wanted to pluck a few fat merchants. We hid behind a wormhole and waited for the tubby to appear. And then, all of a sudden two fleets emerged from the astral depths, an Imperial one and a League one. Nothing's in it, either way, it's not worth powder and shot... So we fled into the wormhole and that's that.
When I came to life, only wreck and corpses were around me. No water, nothing to eat, only warped masts from the ship. Kaput, so to speak. We somehow gathered and made a bonfire. Some of the boys went to find some grub and got lost.
Listen, you are going into the jungle anyway. If you see my guys, tell them that I'll shove a mast down their throat if they don't get back to the camp this instant!
This blasted jungle's giving me the willies... Without a deck below my feet, life sure ain't easy...
Oh, you've found them, the prodigal children, damn them! I am not taught to say thanks. But I swear I owe you one. If we see your tub in the Astral, we won't sink it immediately!
Collect meat, water and fruits and bring them to Bell the Forester on the Rainbow Atoll.

I'm friggin' hungry... My guts have been banging against each other for days in search of food! But there ain't nothing to eat. There's trouble with water as well. All supplies in our barrels have spoiled. Bad news, in a word. I can't leave camp, but without food and water we'll start eating each other soon. I ain't sending my guys into the jungle no more. Half of them are already gone.
Hey, listen... If you find any grub or a flask of fresh water, bring it here right away, ya hear? Meat, fruit... that don't matter! Fruit will be even better - my fangs are gettin' all loose from scurvy. We will repay our debt to you, honest!
Dang! This is enough for a feast! Damn, yo, you really are a savior. Like a... what's his name... Plam the Martyr!
Kill 15 leopards on the Rainbow Atoll and report to Bell the Forester.

Dammit! You hear that? They growl and prowl around our camp... Demons take those flea-covered felines! I remember when we landed at Koch-Itzmahl. It also had many overgrown cats. I got myself a stylish tiger pelt overcoat then!
But that's when we had a full crew, armed and armored. Here my only weapons are a fist and some dirty words. Ain't the same thing...
Lookit, you've got a real weapon on you. How 'bout a business proposition? Chase these spotted tigers outta here before they gobble up one of mine. I will thank you as I can!
I hate cats. I hate dogs, too. Any beasts with fangs, actually. D'you know who I don't hate? Parrots! A parrot sits on your shoulder, curses and chomps on seeds. A true orc in spirit!

Oh, listen, kitties don't growl anymore. Damn! Too bad I don't have gold to pay you. So take this. We'll see each other again, if the Astral permits. Then I will fully repay my debt. My word as a pirate!
Kill 10 Ogres on the Rainbow Atoll and free 5 imprisoned pirates. Then return to Reya the Merciless.

Oh... Don't fuss, landlubber, it's bad enough here... Were you sent by that fat bastard Bell? Sea urchin up his arse! Probably he's sitting up in the camp, drying his underwear, while we're being devoured by ogres. Bastard! If I get back in one piece, I'll scratch his eyes out!
Anyway, my name is Reya. I led the boarding crew on our ship. When we crashed from the skies, I gathered our toughest guys and went scouting the jungle. Who knew that this place was inhabited by ogres, in addition to leopards and monkeys? Real life ogres, no joke! They caught us like we were little kids. Cornered us in the brush and started beatin' on us with clubs. The lucky ones died right then. Maybe they'll even be resurrected. Some were gnawed at a bit, but that's no biggie. A pirate isn't a pirate without a peg leg! But for those who were taken captive, their fate looks much bleaker. If the ogres stuff 'em with garlic and gobble 'em up with salt and pepper, hell if any of them are going to resurrect!
Look, I'm in no condition to fight. They left me for dead here. Save my guys, won't you? We may be pirates, but we don't deserve such a vile death. If you want, you can kill or free them, but don't let them be eaten by ogres! I beg you!
Well, were you able to save my guys from disgraceful death?

This is how you start believing in fairy tales. At the last moment, a handsome prince appears and rescues the princess. Now, I'm not exactly a princess, but then again you ain't much of a prince either. So, our little fairy tale seems rather... off. Anyway, thank you... for everything. If I'll see you again, I'll reward you handsomely, Astral permitting!
Look around the Badger Island and find the source of the explosion that workers and guards talked about.

Do you at least believe us? You don't... I see it in your eyes, you don't! But we are certain there was a ship. The Elf also sent you for some garbage, such as stones and bones, and then refused to admit he ordered you to do it! Are you going to deny what happened? Didn't think so!
We should go to Badger Island and see what's what. Except that we are forbidden from leaving the camp. The admirals say that loose lips sink ships. But I don't see any functional ships around here, only morays...
Listen, let's have you go to the Badger Island and check what exploded there? What if you find that very ship there?

Hurray! You've found us! You are from the rescue team, are you not?
What do you mean "not a rescuer"? We told the admirals that even if this tub were to fly, it wouldn't be for long. But together with that scientist, they kept repeating that it was super important to ascertain coordinates and find out what was wrong with the local Astral... So here we are, dammit! As soon as we departed from the shore and made one turn, our reactor failed. We immediately began to steer toward the shore, but it was too late. The reactor exploded and we fell from the skies onto this sinful earth. The aft was smashed and only a burnt service cap was left of the captain... Oh ho, he probably won't resurrect now! A sad flight to end a career on...
So, no one thought to send a rescue for us? Did they forget about us?!
Gather pages of the ship's log from Cuttleship, which crashed on the Badger Island, and bring them to the Ropemaker Family.

Strange things you are saying. The admiral himself ordered us to fly. We remember it for sure! We even made a note in the ship's log that we bear no liability, since we are obeying the order of a superior officer. The ship was barely functional, and now it's nothing but a pile of metal.
You don't believe us? Here is the ship's log... Oh! Only the cover is left from the log. All the pages must have been dispersed by the wind.
We can't leave the equipment we're responsible for, even if it's all one big wreck at this point. We will sit tight and wait for the rescue team. Someone in the camp has to start wondering about a missing ship, for crying out loud! And you, if you don't believe us, can gather all the missing pages. You'll read for yourself the take-off entry and the flight's objective. That note will confirm our words!

They forgot about us... Did they go mad? How can you forget about a whole ship? We knew they shouldn't have started brewing booze from the local fruit. That must be the reason no one remembers anything!

And here is the last page. There's the official entry, as per protocol. "The ship Cuttlefish departs to conduct visual observation of the shores of an unknown allod and to collect information about a potential enemy." Signed: Admirals of the strike squadron of the first fleet of the League, the Chubby Family. You cannot forge their seal!
This is some kind of nonsense... We were sent to study the Astral! And the date is strange, it is a yesterday's entry. What the deuce!
Bring the ship's log to the Prying Family in the League camp near the Green Cape.

This is unbelievable. Does it mean that all three of us lost our minds? Too bad our guys aren't back from the Purgatory yet, they would have most certainly confirmed our words! We weren't sent on patrol, but on a scientific mission to observe the nearby Astral and learn about its structure. We remember the Elf waving his arms at our captain and making scary eyes, talking about the dangers of astral anomalies.
We'd love to go back to the camp and grab the Elf by the neck ourselves, but cannot abandon the equipment trusted to us. We are the only men left from the crew! Which means we are responsible for the ship. So we'll just sit tight here until the rescue team comes. But you should take the ship's log and return to the camp. Let them figure out what the hell is going on.
Well, don't torture us, speak! Did you find out anything? We are very curious!
Oh... Oh... How is that? What do you mean, "no research was conducted"? We heard everything ourselves! But the paper does not lie... Or does it? What shall we do now?
Meet Viss Sharp-Spear on the Badger Island.

Quarr, Son of the Wind! Good you're here. I've brought urgent news to the war chief. It's very important. We have found the traitor, the planted chick. The same one that got away from you. We know who it is. It is the damned anarchist. They do not want good or bad government. They only want war. They think no one should tell them what to do. Tagar kual kurrakh!
I will fly to the winged city for help, while Viss will stay to spy on foolish anarchista. Your help will be very useful right now. Viss is hiding in bushes. You should quietly whistle, like the wind among cliffs. He will respond like a seagull cry. Together you will easily defeat anarchists.
Are you a complete fool? Krakharak! Don't you try whistle in your own ear? Why not beating drums, playing horn, or dancing like a rabid bear? It's still not so easy to notice!
Gather 8 Elastic Lianas and bring them to Viss Sharp-Spear on the Badger Island.

Traitorous anarchists are crafty and agile. I watch them. They are very careful bastards, twitching from slightest noise, flying like lightning. Wingless one cannot catch them up. Still, it's good to be quick, but it's better to be smart!
Lianas grow in the jungle. Very durable lianas. No one among the People of the Wind can tear it. Wingless one is strong, you can pluck lianas. I will make durable net from lianas. Traitors entangle themselves in the net and will not escape. Then wingless one will take them to the city and have our chief punish them. The chief will be happy, thank outlander and reward me with the best hen to marry! Wingless one does not need a hen anyway, while I want to bring up chicks.
You should only choose fresh liana. Dry liana will not make a good net.

Ar-karna, wingless one! You've brought good liana. I'll weave a durable net. No traitor will escape. Only if I could weave... but without tools, with just bare talons, it's impossible to weave a good net.
Take away the traveling sack from the monkeys inhabiting the Badger Island, then return it to Viss Sharp-Spear.

While you were plucking lianas, I was spying green traitor's camp. Very careful. So careful, even a monkey did not notice. Insolent monkeys stole my sack, kurrakh kurr them all! There were tools in that sack. Knife, awl, everything is lost!
You have to help me again. We must find monkeys and retrieve the sack. I cannot weave a good net without tools. If I do not catch the traitor, then the whole tribe will laugh at me. Then I'd better not return to the city at all.
Some time ago, badgers inhabited this island. Then monkeys came and no more badgers could live there. Only the badger's name's what's left.
Hurray! You have found a sack. I can now make a net and you will easily capture all anarchists.
Kill 12 Aviak Anarchists on the Badger Island and report your victory to Viss Sharp-Spear.

Monarchy's not something they like. Neither those morons are too enthusiastic about the stupid idea of the red-winged. Freedom is all they want. But their understanding of freedom is impunity. Freedom to steal and kill! Cause nothing but trouble. Now they rob us, now they assault red ones, now they carve nasty words on the rock. What word? I don't want to say it, as it's very, very dirty word. They carved it so hard it took us two weeks to paint over it. These anarchists are plain stupid! If you get rid of those morons, all Children of the Wind will be grateful.
Mother of order, no one to rule, freedom, brotherhood, equality... Malarkey! Without a chief, any people become a herd. Only a sturdy wing of a real chief can show the way into future!
Those idiots lost feathers? That's a good job. People of the Wind will remember this victory.
Find the traitor while fighting aviak anarchists, snare him in the net, and find out what he wanted the Crown of the Wind for.

The net is ready. It's time we should take care of the traitor and find out where the crown is hidden!
You're stronger than me, so you can easily handle anarchists, while I should stay here and make sure the traitor will not flee from the camp. If the traitor tries to escape, I'll cry out loud. You'll sure to hear.
It's crucial not to let the traitor flee. He probably is hiding among other anarchists. As soon as you know that he is the traitor, cast the net, tie his wings, ground him and kick his beak. With his wings tied, the traitor won't escape. And if you tickle his feathers, he'll chirp like nightingale. He'll tell you everything, why he stole the crown and where it is. If we get the Crown of the Wind back, Ko'Chuck will be so delighted!
I don't want to fight. This war is not outlanders' concern.
Why do you interfere in affairs of People of the Wind? You'll never grow wings or understand true nature of our people, no matter what stupid Ko'Chuck say!
Toss the crown into the Astral and tell Ko'Chuck in the aviak town by the Green Cape that the crown was destroyed by anarchists.

An outlander doesn't know our history, our customs... Your name is Son of the Wind, but you still do not understand our people!
The Crown of the Wind is not some nice hat. The Crown of the Wind is a symbol. A symbol of a great power! Lust for power split our people. Glittering Wing wanted a chief. Steel Claw wanted no chief. And we... We only wanted brothers' blood stop flowing like a river! One who gets the crown pronounces himself a sovereign of all the winged ones. The war will erupt with new intensity. The war will have no winners, everyone will lose!
If you want do our people good, destroy the Crown of the Wind. Discard it into ever-hungry void beyond our land, and tell the chief the crown is lost forever. With no crown, he will have no reason to call himself a lawful sovereign. Glittering Wing and Steel Claw will be equal in power, their chiefs will need come to agreement. That will not happen right away, but eventually. I believe it. Then People of the Wind will live in peace again!
I was visited by tattered Chlo Bob-Tailed. He said you've found the traitor's den and fought him. Did you find the Crown of the Wind?

What?! The Crown of the Wind turned to ashes?! This cannot be... It is a great symbol! If Karrok owned the crown, all People of the Wind would bow to their true ruler. Even the Steel Claw would accept our authority. And those who refused, would lose their feathers! There can be only one ruler. People need solid government. And we could create such government, and my people could prosper again... But now we need to negotiate with those stupid red-winged - everyone is fed up with the war...
However, there's no great loss without a small gain. If we did not get hold of the crown, the Steel Claw could not have it either. One problem less. Still, I am grateful to you. Please accept this weapon as a gift. Carrying it is a privilege only given to distinguished warriors!
Kill 8 mosquitoes and 8 finguses, get 8 pieces of Tapir Meat and bring them to the Ropemaker Family at the shipwreck on the Badger Island.

Argh, what a nice ship got wrecked... The flotsam can't just be left here... It's our inventory assets! We're not allowed! Only we're scared guarding the remains of the ship here: the jungle is teeming with strange creatures, and mosquitoes are the stuff of nightmares, they are nearly as big as people. One of them stung Brody, our youngest one, and sucked some two pints of her blood on the spot. We barely brought the poor thing to life. She still stutters!
We can't leave the ship, but we can't bear to stay here any longer either! Pray, help us! Take care of the local beasts and we'll be very grateful to you. Also, we'll report your feats to the headquarters when we get back to the camp. Only we're afraid that's not gonna happen soon...
And yeah, if you come across anything edible, kill it and bring it here, because our bowels are roaring like hell. Our bellies are rumbling so loud that Greta mistook me for a tiger a while ago; we had a hard time getting her off the bowsprit.
Carnation essence is useless against local mosquitoes, you need to pile up crossbow bolts!
Wow, a tenderloin! We'll just smoke it a bit, then add some garlic and pepper to get rid of the tropical sores... Gonna make your mouth water!
Kill the Giant Moray and report to the Ropemaker Family on the Badger Island.

We also spotted a moray around here. A big badass one! Thick as a log and razor-sharp, those teeth can bite off an arm or a leg in an instant. Scary as hell... We were about to stroll around the shallow in search of drowned sailors, but the place was swarming with morays! We bolted outta there so fast we nearly ran up a palm tree. If that moray could be taken care of, that'd be a great relief. That beast must have taken plenty of lives!
Tropical paradise my ass! Whenever I recall the local creatures' teeth, my hair stands on end. That... scares you witless!

Is the beast dead? That's great news!
Whoa, what the hell is that? You say that was in the moray's belly? Let's have a closer look...
Kill 5 Terrifying Morays, gather 5 items that belonged to the crew members, and bring them to the Ropemaker Family at the shipwreck on the Badger Island.

Oh, we're in trouble... That signet belonged to our captain! Does that mean the beast gobbled him up? Holy cow, he won't be able to resurrect now! How dreadful... Goddamned beasts, it's all their fault that our crew died a final death!
Help us avenge our companions. Please! Their souls must not be left unrequited. Should you find any items that belonged to the sailors, bring them to us. At least we'll know who can still resurrect and who should be given funeral rites.
So many fine fellas that died for nothing... Sob...

The ship's cook used to make cakes from old bootlegs that were finger-lickin' good. And the helmsman would steer the ship through anomalies like a thread through a needle's eye. And the chaplain... Argh, no point going on... Suffice it to say we've lost good people! May their memory live forever!
Deliver the Bag of Dead Sailors to the Chubby Family at the League Camp next to the Green Cape.

We can't even bury our companions, seeing as they found their last refuge in the morays' guts. Looks like we'll have to mount gravestones over empty graves. At least we have some of their belongings, that's something to remember them by.
 Please take these items to our admirals and tell them the guys died heroic deaths in the line of duty. Let the dead be given proper respects...
Now, what do you want? Gonna bother us with idle chit-chat again?

What's that trash? Dead crew members' stuff? What the hell are you talking about?! Once again, we didn't have a ship and we didn't send anyone anywhere.
The Ropemaker Family? Never heard of them. Do you engage in alcohol abuse? Or maybe you had a sunstroke?
Get out of here... Go find Maria Divova! She can give you some pills to bring you back to normal, 'cause you're clearly hallucinating!
Ask Mark Gorlov about the situation.

Hey, just don't faint again! I was barely able to revive you! I thought that's it, no more hero... Glory to the Light, you have a strong head.
Wait, relax. Look how wobbly you are. You can barely stand on your feet. You are about to crash. Don't fuss, breathe slowly, let me introduce myself.
My name is Mark Gorlov. I was captain's first mate on the flagship of our strike squardron. Our ship entered the wormhole first... Its remains are over there, floating in the Astral, near the shore. So consider yourself lucky!
Listen carefully, I don't have time to yack with you. There are still plenty of wounded to care for.
So that's that. Now I understand what happened to our fleet. Imagine what happened to common brigantines and corvettes if the League's ships were left in tatters.
Collect barrels of provisions, boxes of tools and coiled ropes that remained after the shipwreck, and bring them to Mark Gorlov at the shipwreck.

I want to ask one more favor of you... We don't have a cargo hold after the shipwreck, while your ship is almost intact. Right now every little thing might help. Salted meat, ropes, nails, hammers, saws - everything! We need to reinforce our camp, or at least to put canopies to live under, and also we don't have much too eat. If you see anything useful, bring it to me immediately, I'll find a use for any and all supplies.
Eh, I could use a keg of beer...
Good! Now that means business! With these instruments and durable ropes we can build a camp in two minutes flat!
Exterminate 10 morays around the shipwreck site and report on the completed task to Chubby Family at the League camp.

Tropics... I hate tropics! Just look at the local sea - the predators are all piled up on top of one another! Truly, this is no tropical resort atoll. The worst I saw was this enormous fish with finger-length teeth! If a beast like that grabs hold of your leg, get ready to limp for the rest of your life. I only saw them before in pictures. Gibberlings call them morays.
I fear that these beasts will start feasting on us... Chase them away! Morays have a cowardly reputation, so if you manage to kill ten of them, the rest will learn to keep their distance.
Whoa! Who bit you like that? Morays? There is no rest from them!

So have you managed to chase morays away? Excellent! Now we can walk in shallow waters without fear of losing our feet. By the way, don't forget to take care of your wounds. Morays' teeth contain all sorts of things. You may even get some disease from their bite.
Question workers and guards in the League camp about the "lost" ship and report results to Inquisitive family in the League camp.

No, we won't let it go! There was a ship! Was! We heard it ourselves! We cannot all be struck by senility simultaneously!
And if the admirals refuse to confess to existence of a ship, maybe the guards or the workers will be more loose-lipped. Except they won't tell us squat. They'll think that the Prying Family have heard another rumor... You, however, they may trust. So you question them.
There was a ship, we know it! Why would they hide it from us? Strange...
Well, what's playing tricks, it is our ears or the admirals' memory?
No one remembers the ship? Impossible! Although there was one worker who mentioned that some ship wrecked near the Badger Island...
Well, what do you want? Say what you need and get out. I have a lot of work.
What ship? Are you talking about that pile of metal that used to be our flagship? It is in the Astral, not far from the camp. I don't know about any other ship.

A ship? Yes, I think one recently crashed here. No, not that one that burns at the shore; I heard a crash from the side of the Badger Island. Or maybe it wasn't a ship. I don't know. If you want, you can go and check for yourself, I have lots of work to do.
Meet the mysterious stranger in the Cave of Elements under Sunny Cascade. But first you will need to receive the Blessing of Elements from an ancient witch who lives on Kahlua Island.

Listen carefully and don't interrupt. And don't stare at me! I am visible only to you, I don't exist to others. So simply shut up and listen.
I know that you've already noticed people's strange memory gaps. That's just the tip of the iceberg. Let's just say it is a small error that made its way into robust calculations of our old acquaintance.
You probably don't remember me? Oh well. It is not important right now. What is important is that you know that you're in great danger. Let's just say that the owner of this paradise is saddened by your unbridled curiosity and wishes to get rid of you. Don't believe your eyes: everything surrounding you is a trap for naive fools, and the trap door just shut itself. Whether you believe me or not is up to you. But if you want to survive, then meet me in a place called the Cave of Elements, and I will show you just how deep the rabbit hole goes.
For a moment I thought you would not come. Well, you made the right choice. I am not disappointed in you.
Revive 5 fainted sailors and question them as to the shipwreck cause. Report on the addition to the Chubby Family in the League camp.

Well, how do you feel? No longer dizzy? Great! Since you are all right, then help me revive the other survivors. The impact was so strong that the boarding crew from the upper deck was cast everywhere along the shore. I pray to Tensess that our guys are all right.
Go, find survivors, revive them and send them here. I'll tend to their wounds. And question those who are conscious. Perhaps they saw something that may explain the cause of the shipwreck.
Hello-hello! Are you from the ship that wrecked nearby?
Too bad not everyone was lucky enough to survive... But you are good! First you tend to others, only then to yourself. Respect!
Tell the Chubby Family at the League camp about the sailor's suspicions.

Cough... My lungs are full of water... I thought I would die for sure!
Hey, didn't you have an Imperial uniform on you? Yes, you did! I remember! When the ship crashed, I fell overboard into the water. I remember vividly: everything became a blur, folks screaming horribly, fire everywhere, and you standing over me in an Imperial uniform. I thought that the Imperials came to our rescue... and then I fainted. When I came to life, you had another set of clothes on.
Hold on... If it wasn't you, then the Imperials knew beforehand that our ship would crash and explode? Then why would someone in an Imperial uniform be around right after the shipwreck? It must be their handiwork! They must have lured us here and caused the crash! We need to tell everything to our leader immediately!

So that's how it is? Oh, good thing we did not trust those damn Imperials! If it was a trap, then Kania is facing a serious threat. Oh man... We were fools to agree to this venture! We must contact Aidenus immediately!
Track down and kill the Imperial spy near the League camp and report your success to the Chubby Family.

So that's how it is. Act with our own forces and without support. And with the Empire throwing monkey wrenches our way. We don't have a clue whether Tep was involved in what happened, but there's no way we wouldn't know if it was the Committee! Damned traitors! We'd strangle all of them with our bare paws!
With all the running around trying to establish communication, we totally forgot about what one of the sailors told you. Do you remember? If his memory is true, then he saw a live Imperial in our area. And our sentries reported some creature hiding in bushes near the camp, which fled as soon as they cocked their crossbows. What wild animal would know a crossbow?! It must have been an Imperial spy, and he is hiding somewhere near.
We ask you to find him and kill him! Traitors must remain ignorant!
So, did the Imperial bastard get what he deserved?
What do you mean "the Empire is innocent"?! How can they not be guilty? They were the ones to lure us here!
Meet the aviak shaman, Whew Black-Feather, in the aviak village on the Green Cape.

Well... If the Empire wants a war, then they'll get a war! We also have an ace up our sleeve. And this ace is locals!
Don't you know? Oh, our empty heads! We forgot to tell you the most important thing! We recently made contact with the locals and were able to find common ground. They are aviaks! Frankly, they are some strange aviaks. Wild and illiterate. But they fully agree with our ideas! And for sure they won't support the damned Imperials.
Why, you ask? It's simple! If we understood correctly, there was a schism in the aviak tribe. Separatists under red banners attempted to start a revolution but were defeated and forever banished from the tribe to the other side of the island! The locals call that land Irdrich, by the way.
Whoa, mama... The Imperials landed on that side of the island! What if they ally with these revolutionaries? Alarm! We have to immediately inform our new friends!
Quickly run to the aviak village, find their shaman and tell him that reds may return with reinforcements.

Quarr, wingless!
What brought you outlander to our village? All kind of winds blow through here, but we are happy to see new friends!
You heart is closed to the song of the wind... I see it. He who cannot fly never can understand our people. If wingless one wants friendship, you must obtain wings. Outlander should go to Cheeba and learn, then return, only then we can talk!
Find a traitor among young white aviaks inhabiting the edge of the Green Cape, then return to Ko'Chuck in the Glittering Wing village on the Green Cape.

So did you find this symbol at Ktar-Karkh? Outlanders also call it Deadman's Rock. Did you find it on the ground in the other outlanders' camp? Strange, but I believe you. You have no reason to lie.
I want to say one thing to you. Promise you won't tell anyone. It's a big secret! We were transporting a treasure of the old capital. Wind Crown! A symbol of a true ruler! Since long ago, the crown belonged to the ruler, a king of aviaks. If Karrok equipped the crown, his power would increase significantly. Reds would be scared, and whites would show respect and fight reds better. But it was not given to him...
The crown was stolen by the reds long time ago. We recently retrieved it, older aviaks stayed behind to protect it from chase, younger ones carried the crown to the village. But I think there is a traitor among the young ones. A planted chick! He wears white feathers, but he is red. Will you help me find him? Youngsters do not know you, so they won't be surprised by your questions. An outlander is an outlander, after all. You will find the traitor and find out where he carried off the crown.
Young aviaks do not live in town. They live on the edge of the cape, nest in a big house, until they become real men. You should go there, ask around, look around, find a planted chick, and report to me. Try not to scare him. We need him alive!

He escaped? How could you let him get away? You are strong and agile... A young aviak could not overcome you!
Oh well, let him be. You say that a planted chick fled towards the Badger Island? Then I give him chase. We'll find him and interrogate him ourselves. You needn't do anything else. I'll deal with everything myself. In any case, I am grateful. Perhaps the traitor escaped, but I will not repeat that mistake again!
Quarr, outlander! What brought a wingless one to our house?
Ouch! Did you lose your mind? That hurts! Have you never seen white feathers before?

Damn it! You cracked me, yes? Yet you're dumb, you don't understand anything. We are doing good deeds, but you outlander spoiled everything. I'll leave now; if you try to stop me, I'll kill you and escape.
Meet Jean-Jacques de Desirae in the League camp near the Green Cape.

Oh, I was just going to look for you. Have you met Jean-Jacques? He is such a dearie! Can you imagine that he promised to name an allod after me, should he discover one? What a man!
Oh, excuse me, I digress. Jean-Jacques asked me to find someone with strong muscles who could help him with his research. He is so smart, he knows everything! And if he doesn't know something, he knows just what to do to find the answer. It is a great pleasure to work with him!

Greetings! What can I do for you?
Maria sent you? Hm... I actually asked her to send me an available sailor and not to bother busy people. But the thoughtless dame mixed up everything again...
Oh well, since you're volunteering to help, I am not going to reject it.
Record measurements at the indicated locations and report to Jean-Jacques de Desirae in the League camp.

I admit, I am totally confused! I dedicated my whole life to exploring the Astral! Not many people understand the Astral. Everyone considers it fatally dangerous element, but I worship it. It is beautiful! Look into the Astral, feel its breath and pulse. It is eternal and ever-changing, beautiful and terrible as nothing else; it gives birth and death... It's wonderful!
But the local Astral looks... different. It is dead and cold. I don't sense in it any primeval and wild energy which overflows the Astral in any other sector of any layer. And that wormhole through which we ended up here... I don't see any exit from it in the sky. But we are alive, which means it must open directly above the island. And that simply cannot be! The allod would have been blown to pieces and absorbed by the Astral long ago due to such close proximity to the wormhole.
I have some theories, but without facts they are nothing. I need precise data, and I would like you to collect it. Take my measuring device. It is already calibrated. All you have to do is press this green button. Record measurements in several places on the astral shore and return to me with the data. Let's not waste any more time.
Have you ever seen an astral storm? It's quite a rare sight. Mesmerizing and deadly! One who survives such a storm never forgets it.

Measurements ready? Good, just in time. I've already constructed an approximate matrix which can shed light on the nature of the local Astral, but I need precise data, not a crystal ball. Fortune telling is Barisheva's job, while astral studies are precise science!
Collect 5 fish bone fragments, 5 crooked beaks, 5 turtle shells and 5 stones warped by the Astral. Bring them to Jean-Jacques de Desirae in the League camp near the Green Cape.

It is impossible! Here, look - the first reading has zero voltage, while the second goes beyond all tolerable limits, and yet the allod somehow remains intact. The third reading has a negative value! It is im-pos-si-ble! No way. No how. Theoretically.
Equipment looks operational... I think I haven't gone mad yet. Readings were done exactly per instructions. I set all the parameters on the measuring device myself. What if I was given defective equipment, which some paper-pusher approved as operational? When I return home, I'll rip the procurement agents' heads off, encase them in formaldehyde and create an impressionist exhibition entitled "Triumph of Greed Over Common Sense." But that's going to happen later. Right now we will perform our research using old school methods - with materials touched by the Astral. Just for that, I have samples of astral amber, collected in Darkwater. A comparison of parameter deviations of that matter with the local samples should help me solve this mystery.
I will start preparing the necessary equipment right away, and you, if it is not too difficult, should start collecting samples. For research I will need something mineral, i.e. stones or crystals that are strewn about the shore. I will also need various living samples, such as bird beaks, fish bones or turtle shells. In a word, any hard organic material that hasn't been subjected to decay.
I hope that by setting parameters for local astral warping we will understand how to get out of this cursed sector... I truly hope so!
So, fifteen for tolerance, minus hundred eleven... Subtract the division of matrix from the constant, add a differentiated variable... Well, what do you have?

Samples? What kind of garbage is this? I didn't order that!
What do you mean "device was broken and I asked to collect samples"? I never asked you to collect this trash!
Were you, by chance, concussed during the shipwreck? Any memory gaps? None of my equipment is faulty! Everything works properly! I am processing data as we speak, though I already see that everything is within norm. This local Astral is no different from a regular one.
...
Cut it out - I never sent you for any samples! Read my lips: did not send! My trained intellect remembers everything in detail. Aside from readings, I did not expect anything else from you. The readings were adequate, the data was accurate, and the result was perfectly expected.
That's it, now go away and don't bother me with your nonsense. Better yet, see the ship's doctor and let him check your head for brain trauma. What nerve! Accusing me, an outstanding researcher and scientist, of amnesia!
Question the Chubby Family about the fate of the ship that survived the wormhole and return to the Prying Family.

Hey! Psst! Listen to what we say. Please forgive us for eavesdropping on your conversation with the elf. We did not do it on purpose, honest. It is just that we are too inquisitive. They even call us like that, the Prying Family.
We think that something strange is going on. You are not the first to encounter similar forgetfulness. We, for example, heard with our own ears that Jean-Jacques proposed to admirals to send the sole surviving ship to circle the island. It happened before your arrival here, but now everybody is sure that no ship has survived. But we heard it with our own ears! Honest!
Listen, our admirals trust you. Try to tell them our suspicions. Just don't tell them that we were eavesdropping, otherwise we'll be punished...
Well, were you able to extract anything interesting from the admirals?
What? How so? We heard about the ship ourselves... Honest, we are not lying. Amazing...
Bring 20 tree-frog legs and 10 beakers of tree-frog slime to Maria Divova in the League camp near the Green Cape.

Oh, hello! You are probably one of those who were sent to search for us? We got in trouble! We got stuck here, like a bone in a throat, neither in nor out... Oh well. We've been through worse jams than this, so we'll be all right! Come to think of it, it is not that bad here. Local aviaks are pleasant enough, even though they are savages. The important thing is that they understand that a steady hand and strict authority, without extra committees and bureaucracy, can be effective. Except that their king is ailing. I am not sure whether he was wounded in battle or ate a rotten fish. I don't understand their chirping much. But I think that if we can heal their king, the locals will be much friendlier to us.
Well, would you like to help me in a noble cause of saving the leader of a friendly country, even if their country is the size of this island? Then catch me some local frogs, please. They are awfully repulsive! I've been afraid of these creatures since childhood, but I cannot make a magical elixir without their legs. You don't have to bring me whole frogs. All I need is twenty frog legs and ten beakers with their slime.

Just don't grab them with your bare hands. Local frogs are terribly poisonous, and I have neither anesthesia nor antidote. If you get bit, we'll have to amputate the extremity all the way to the neck! It is an age old method!

Whoa, such scrumptious legs! These frogs must have been huge. This is just what I need for the potion.
Now I will boil them, dry them, and make a potion from their slime... It'll treat any illness!
Add 10 doses of snake venom into the beaker with the potion, then bring it to Karrok Stout-Hearted in the Glittering Wing village on the Green Cape.

Oh, my forgetful head! I completely forgot! The main potion component is venom of a tropical horned viper. Without it, this potion was and will remain poisonous. But with that venom... Do you know the proverb: "Treat like with like"? This is exactly how this potion works. Snake venom neutralizes the toxins in tree-frog slime, and the resulting compound, when it enters the patient's body, forces them to fight the illness with all of the might, and defeat it.
Don't you want to save the chief of our new friends? Then help me complete my task. The beaker that I gave you contains an almost prepared potion. All you need to do is add snake venom, ten doses, and have the chief drink the mixture. I hope I calculated dosage correctly...
Quarr... I asked you not to bother me...
What? Young lady with blond feathers on her head wants to treat me? Kha... She thinks she can treat children of the Wind?
Taste the healing potion and tell Karrok Stout-Hearted about your sensations.

It's not that I don't believe you... But this mixture stinks so much! I don't even want to know what's inside. Tak-taq arrawakh... I really doubt the medicinal power of this stinky liquid. I think that beaker will crack from stench soon.
Are you sure it will help? No? Then you better drink first. Just a little bit. Just one sip. If you're fine, then I'll drink as well. Don't be offended, but I did not become chief by being a naive chick, quetal-kul!
First you drink, then I will. If you survive, that is.

Kukhul taq-taggar! are you all right? I was afraid that you had already gone to heaven to eternally fly with the free wind and never return to the sinful earth. I do not want to drink this gross mixture. You better spill it into the deepest hole on the most remote island and never bring it up. And tell that wingless torturer that chief is feeling much better. I'm not lying! I saw you bend in pain and I immediately felt will to live!
Collect 10 stems of Emerald Arrowhead and 10 Kurru Berries on the Green Cape and return to Whew Black-Feather in the Glittering Wing village.

I've heard you want to receive wings, wingless one. Then you will become a swore brother to People of the Wind! From then on, you will be called Son of the Wind. A son always helps his father, does not he? Then you will help us!
Father of People of the Heavens, Karrok Stout-Hearted, is wise and strong, but he's ill. Very ill. When we fought with the damned red rebels, Karrok flew in the vanguard! He led our tribe in battle! An arrow hit him right in chest. Now Karrok is really sick. Between life and death. And a new Son of the Wind can help me cure him.
Go into forest to find kurru berries and emerald arrowhead. Kurru berries are very poisonous. You can die if you swallow even one. Arrowhead is useful and medicinal. It treats wounds, cough, and infertility. It treats everything! Combined together, they are strong enough even to resurrect a corpse.
Gather berries carefully. Juice is also poisonous. If you burn yourself with juice, apply an arrowhead right away. It will extract poison and save you.
You've done a great job. You've found juicy berries and the emerald arrowhead. Thank you, Son of the Wind!
Collect a large Turtle Shell and 10 chunks of Turtle Meat. Return to Whew Black-Feather in the Glittering Wing village.

Now I have another task for you. I heard that you can swim. That's good. We, people of the Wind, can fly, but we swim badly and only down. I need a cover and meat of a sea stone. You call it something different, not a sea stone, but I don't remember. Why do I need a difficult word when there is a simple one? A sea stone is a stone. It swims and eats and, when in danger, it hides inside a stone. Dive into the water, catch the sea stone and bring it here. I'll make an amulet out of its cover!
A sea stone is tasty. Just it's so difficult to catch. One must take it very high in the sky and then drop on the ground. Then a sea stone lose its cover and is tasty.

I remember how wingless ones call a sea stone! Tattle! No? Toottle? No... Got it! Turtle!
Wingless ones speak a tongue-twisting language! My beak hurts.
Using an amulet, create a sacrificial circle, kill 10 leopards while in the circle, and return to Karrok Stout-Hearted in the Glittering Wing village.

A powerful amulet can be made from hydra teeth. Son of the Wind, you're almost done, wash the amulet in sacrificial blood of a powerful enemy. Then a spirit will hide in the amulet. Chief will wear the amulet and the spirit will protect the chief. It protects from illness, sickness, even death... With luck.
Taq-kuarr, Son of the Wind! The Chief's life is in your talons. Take the amulet and go hunting into the forest. Powerful, fierce and agile leopards inhabit it. Strong spirit, taq-taggar! When you touch the amulet, it will draw a sacrificial circle. If you kill a leopard inside the circle, its spirit will inhabit the amulet. Then you can give the amulet to Karrok. The Chief will wear the amulet and become completely healthy!
Heaven loves you Son of the Wind. I have faith in your success! Qual-kutarr!
Cough... Cough... What do you want from an old and sick aviak, chick?

Amulet? Old Whew completely lost his mind... Oh well, give it here. Amulet won't hurt, I think...
...
Taq-taggar! I think it's working. I feel... better! Quar-caw, chick. You saved me! My honor tells me, not many winged ones would risk their lives for an outlander. But you, wingless one, risked and saved me without hope for gratitude! You are very noble, my friend. I don't speak for all your people, but you are always welcomed in my home!
I wish to reward you. This reward cannot compare to what you do for me, but I think it will be useful in your travel through our land.
Throw a poisoned bait to the nightmarish hydra, wait until the poison works, kill the hydra, take its tooth and hide, and bring them to Whew Black-Feather in the Glittering Wing village.

You are just wonderful! You collected poison berries, sea stone's cover and meat. No question was asked. I had a hidden agenda when asked for those items. I'll make a potion from herbs that eliminate pain and give it to Karrok. And others go toward a poisonous bait. It will be a very tasty bait! I'd eat it myself if not for poison. A hydra is stupid, knows nothing about the poison. What hydra, you ask? A hydra that you are going to kill.
Hydras live on a small island near our village. Hydras are strong, but stupid. Throw the bait at it and a hydra will swallow it, and then get very ill from poison. Kill that hydra, collect its teeth and hide, and bring them to me. I'll make a powerful amulet out of them!
Hydra is strong, Son of the Wind is quick, but old Whew is crafty! Craftiness and agility always trump dumb strength.

Good hide! I'll make a hat out of it. You're a good hunter, you have the right to wear the hat made from hydra. Beautiful hat!
I'll make an amulet out of teeth, summon a powerful spirit, bind it to the amulet, and give it to Karrok. The spirit will chase away sickness and make the Chief healthy!
Kill zombies that attacked an aviak platoon on the road leading to the Deadman's Rock, and find the valuable thing lost by white aviaks.

Quarr, friend of Glittering Wing. People of the Wind talk much about your deeds. They say you strangled the Swamp Terror, the gigantic hydra that ate many good warriors, with your bare hands. They say you know martial art of other people, other land, and that is how you win. I think it will be easy for you to fulfill my request.
Our platoon was going to the east of the village, carrying a valuable item there. Then someone attacked the platoon, consisted mainly of chicks... young and dumb chicks. They were afraid to fight and fled from battle. They flew into the village and talked about strange things.
They say the platoon walked at night. Red enemies were not asleep, looking to sabotage. Workers! Proletariat! Damn their taq-taggar... Except our warriors did not meet reds, but someone else. Chicks say they were walking stealthily. They did not see anything at night. And then a bright light shone on them, a box where outlanders bury the dead flew in the air above the road. And zombies with scythes were standing along the road... And complete silence!
I want to ask you, go and see what happened to platoon. Our warriors are brave, but they are afraid of the dead. Will you check? I'll be grateful!
By the looks of it, this is that very box with the valuable item inside that Ko'Chuck was talking about...
The valuable item is gone. Carried off. Where will it be found?
Track down the robbers and find out their fate. Relay the news to Ko'Chuck Water-Fowl in the Glittering Wing village on the Green Cape.

Shoe tracks near the box lead deep into the jungle. The robbers that routed the platoon of white aviaks did not bother to cover their tracks. Perhaps it makes sense to follow them and find out where the hapless robbers hid, and also look for evidence that may shed light on one question: why would the Arisen attack an aviak platoon?
Did you find out what scared our chicks?

You talk strange things. Arisen? I do not know them. Our dead never roam the earth. There are no other outlanders besides you. Where did the dead come from? That's a mystery.
And here's an interesting feather you found. It tells me many things. But I tell you about it some other time. I don't want to make a mistake, understand? The matter is too important to... tal-kutul, how you say it... poke a finger at the sky? A very wise word. Return later, when I stop thinking and start talking. Agree?
You have found shreds of Imperial military uniform near the bones.
Find traces of the Empire's citizens on the Deadman's Rock and report your findings to Yaroslav Kramov, who's waiting in the settlement of the Glittering Wing tribe.

Well met, friend! I heard a lot about your feats. And, well, I envy you. You know how to win others' trust! By the way, it's trust I wanna talk to you about. Trust between us and our little winged allies, or, to be more precise, the absence of it. Why do you think their leader told you nothing about the valuable cargo? They don't seem to trust you... And a lack of trust is a step away from enmity.
Looks like their honcho blames us for the loss. While I'm sure it's the Empire's doing. The Arisen didn't turn up here by chance! Those bastards must be plotting something. And if we don't keep our eyes open, we're gonna be in trouble. Now more than ever, we need a solid alliance with the natives. This is why I order you to find the aviaks' loss by any means necessary. If the Empire really is behind it, as I suspect, make sure the natives know all about it.
If I understand correctly, the aviaks were attacked in the vicinity of the Deadman's Rock, right? What are you waiting for, then?! We should have combed the island and looked under every boulder long ago. They must have left a trail!
So, is the news good or bad?

Wow! I'll be damned... That's a tribal sign of the aviaks, their warriors put it on the wing. And this camp doesn't look like our scouts stayed in it. The Empire may have banded together with the aviaks. However, I don't wanna slander them without proof. After all, what if I'm wrong?
Catch 25 crabs with the net and bring them to Alarik Falcon-Eye on the Deadman's Rock.

Quarr, outlander! I heard the wind speak. Wind loves you! Wind tells a lot to the one who can hear. Wind says you are very, very fast. You have a keen eye and a steady hand. Skilled hunter, yes? Can you hunt agile crabs, wingless one? No? How can it be? I'll teach you!
Take the net and go along the beach, wingless one. Crabs are e very agile, catching them is not easy. You should cast a net, wingless one. A crab will get into it and stop running. Then the crab is easy to catch. Toss it into the pot right away! The crab will turned red, and adding cane tincture will make it much tastier.
Crabs are agile, but I'm crafty. I was the first to figure out how to catch crabs with a net. The whole thanked me.

Crabs! Many crabs! Wind speaks the truth - hunting spirits and a wingless outlander are gracious. Thank you. I'll wrap crabs in raw leaves, put them in the net and take them to the village. They will cook crabs and maize broth, and add cane tincture... It would be delicious!
Check the snares set on the Deadman's Rock, get 10 Singing Birds and bring them to Alarik Falcon-Eye.

I have another favor to ask. I set snares everywhere on the cliff. I wanted to catch singing birds. Aviak ladies like singing birds a lot. They also like lucky hunters who catch birds. Though I'm not so lucky. Birds got into snares and sat quiet. As soon as I fly near, birds thrash their wings, try flying away... Snares are strong and birds are dumb - they often die from fear! But you - you walk silently. No wings, no wind. Birds will not fear a wingless one. Take them carefully out of snares them to me. I'll make bouquets, tie to birds' feet and give them to ladies. They will favor mecook crabs for me and serve maize broth and cane tincture. Celebrate!
Do not eat birds, wingless outlander! Do not eat singing birds, listen to them. If a bird starts singing in your belly, it will scare away the whole village. The sound will be just horrible...
You've been a great help, wingless one. Now, I will make huge bouquets and give them to ladies. They will favor me very much.
Get 10 Crocodile Hides and 20 Crocodile Fangs. Bring the trophies to Alarik Falcon-Eye on the Deadman's Rock.

I completely forgot! The Chief did not send me to catch birds. Not even delicious crabs. The Chief wanted a strong hide and sharp fangs. A hide to make armor and fangs to make amulets, arrowheads and sharp knives. I'm such a fool, I was thinking about ladies... If I return without a hide and fangs, the Chief will skin me and use my hide to make a tambourine! Poor, poor me. A bird is done for...
I don't want to bother my wingless friend anymore. But I don't want to lose my skin either. I offer a deal - you will help me get the hide and fangs. A good thing to do and a good reward to get!
Armored crocodiles have the best hides and fangs. Tough like a rock!

I'm saved! You got half of hides and fangs, I got the other half. Now I'll give hides and fangs to the Chief and then go to ladies to listen to singing birds and have delicious crab with cane tincture. I am so happy! You should take this reward and not refuse. Keep it as a memory!
Bang the gong on top of the Green Cape and summon a tamed squawker. Use it to go to the top of the Giant's Claw, steal a squawker's egg and go back to Cheebah One-Eye at the Green Cape.

Quetal quarr, outlander! What brought a wingless one to Cheebah? Do you want to learn? Then I'll teach you!
Have you ever heard of squawkers, outlander? I'll explain. A squawker is a bird. Toothy, powerful and always hungry. Very smart, but very angry. It's hard to tame. But a squawker flies like lightning, faster than wind! If you want to understand People of the Wind, you should tame a squawker. A mature squawker cannot be tamed, it's completely wild. You must find a small squawkling and tame it. Feed and care for it... Then a squawker will grow big and fly you on its back. Then you wingless one will become winged and understand our people!
Now climb the mountain and hit the gong. A tamed squawker knows the gong's sound well. Every island has its own gong. As soon as a squawker swoops in, climb atop it and fly to Giant's Claw. Wild and angry squawkers live there. Look for a squawker's egg, then strike the gong and bring the egg back. I will then help you hitch... hooch... tell you what to do.
Outlander, I sent you to bring a squawker's egg. Did you find one?
That's good! I know what to do about the egg. You should wait. Wait just a little.
Feed 20 pieces of meat to the squawkling and get back to Cheebah One-Eye at the Green Cape.

Wingless one, listen to me now. I'll give you a bone whistle. Blow this whistle, wingless one, and a squawkling will come. It will be small. Hungry. Gonna eat like hell! A squawker is not a parrot, it doesn't eat fruit. Only meat.
Go hunting, outlander, to get meat and feed a squawkling. When it grows very big, it will love you like its parent. It will carry you on its back up high in the sky! You will understand, trust us and make friends with our people!
If you feed squawker well, it love you and fly you high. But if you not feed it well, it might become angry and bite you.

Quamool qootlack, Wingless Outlander! A squawker for Wingless equals to wings. Now Wingless can bang the Gong on any island and call a squawker. A squawker will fly to the gong, fly high and fast. And Wingless will become Son of the Wind!
Meet with Marrianne de Ardeur in the church in Novograd's Main Square.

Hello! Forgive me for distracting you from your heroic deeds, but I have an urgent order that can't wait.
Marianne de Ardeur, abbess of the Church of Light, wants to see you. Looks like something came up... I don't know what exactly, though.
Now hurry to Marianne, she wouldn't summon a League hero for nothing!
Oh, there you are! Strange things happen in the world after Master was defeated by the heroes of Sarnaut... I'm afraid that by slaying him we pushed the world closer to the brink!
